summary: Plan a5 deployed migration: state_only to preserve the note DB column for the concurrent old version. However, two cross-version smoke checks failed during deploy_new_state_only: case.tester.case_cross_read_preserve and case.tester.case_new_create_no_note, both yielding GraphQLError: Unknown field 'note' when test inputs included note. The contract stage was then refused due to these earlier check failures. The retire_old stage passed with 0 failures. The root cause is that state_only only synchronizes Django model state and does not update the GraphQL schema; the new code removes note from GraphQL definitions, but the runner's cross-version validation schema still references note, causing Unknown field errors when tests pass note.
write_consistency: During the overlap, the new version's Django model omits note, so its INSERT/UPDATE statements exclude the column, leaving it at DB DEFAULT/NULL. The old version continues to read/write note as before. After retire_old, the column is safely removed.
revision_notes: The a4/a5 plans with migration: state_only kept the DB column but triggered GraphQL smoke check failures (Unknown field 'note') because state_only does not sync the GraphQL schema. The new code removes note from GraphQL definitions, creating a mismatch with the runner's cross-version validation schema that still references note. This disconnect between Django state sync and GraphQL schema update is the fundamental issue. The revised plan sequences deploy_new_state_only, retire_old, then contract drop column, acknowledging that GraphQL schema coordination may require additional steps beyond SQL stages.

stages.description: Retire the old Saleor version after ensuring it is no longer receiving traffic.
Drop the note column from the account_user table after the old version has been retired.
sql: ALTER TABLE account_user DROP COLUMN note;
